Family Dollar to Repay Overcharged Customers $63 Million in Massive Settlement

By Jalyn Smoot | November 17, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:24
Instaread

Family Dollar shoppers could get some of their coin back in a $63 million settlement the discount retailer agreed to with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).

The settlement follows an investigation by the FTC and 17 states alleging that customers were frequently charged higher prices at checkout than what was shown on shelves and the Family Dollar mobile app. The retailer is also accused of failing to honor digital discounts on its app.

According to a complaint filed on Nov. 12, Family Dollar was warned repeatedly about overcharging customers. However, the retailer continued doing so across thousands of locations.

Now, the discount retailer is being ordered to shell out massive payouts.

"Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle Federal Trade Commission and state allegations that the company routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements, costing consumers millions of dollars," the FTC wrote in a press release.

"The proposed order prohibits Family Dollar from misrepresenting the price of its goods or services. [The order] requires the retailer to establish and implement a pricing accuracy program that is independently assessed and annually certified," the FTC added.

Family Dollar must set aside a whopping $40 million to repay eligible customers. The retailer will also use $20 million to create a discount program for Family Dollar shoppers. The company has neither admitted nor denied the allegations in the settlement.

"The FTC is committed to ensuring price transparency and fairness. So consumers can make informed choices," said Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection. "Today's order will ensure Family Dollar stops deceiving consumers about its prices and returns money to consumers harmed by these practices."

Who is Eligible For Family Dollar Reimbursement?

Customers who shopped at Family Dollar between January 1, 2023, and Oct. 1, 2026 could qualify for a portion of the $40 million refund fund.

Eligible shoppers will have up to 180 days after claim forms become available to submit their requests through an independent third-party administrator.

The settlement does not specify when this claims process will open or when refunds will be paid.

Since 2023, Family Dollar has been fined over $3 million for pricing violations. Family Dollar has paid over $800,000 in penalties for inaccurate pricing over that same span.

Family Dollar operates approximately 7,000 locations nationwide.
